09:30

Masala omelette and guacamole toast

10 minutes

474 kcal · 37 g protein · 40 g carbs · 19 g fat · 9 g fibre

Ingredients
ItemWeightNote
Whole egg50 g1 whole egg
Egg whites165 gwhites of 5 eggs
Spinach (palak)30 gchopped
Onion25 gfinely chopped
Tomato30 gdeseeded
Bell pepper30 gdiced
Green chilli2 g
Coriander leaves3 g
Olive oil, extra virgin3 gnon-stick pan
Whole wheat bread60 g2 slices, toasted
Signature Guacamole45 gspread on the toast
Almonds10 gabout 8, soaked overnight and peeled
  1. Whisk the egg and the 5 whites with a pinch of salt, pepper and haldi.
  2. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan. Soften onion, pepper and chilli for 2 minutes, then add spinach and tomato for 30 seconds.
  3. Pour in the eggs and cook on medium-low for 2 to 3 minutes. Fold, and finish with coriander.
  4. Toast the bread and spread the guacamole. Peel the soaked almonds and eat them alongside.

12:30

Office lunch

Eaten at the office

522 kcal · 33 g protein · 70 g carbs · 14 g fat · 14 g fibre

Ingredients
ItemWeightNote
Whole wheat atta25 g1 phulka, no ghee (or 75 g cooked rice, not both)
Yellow moong dal (dry)30 g1 katori dal, about 150 g cooked
Kala chana, boiled70 g1 katori chana, rajma, soya or paneer curry; 29 g dry
Sunflower oil8 gcooking oil in dal and curry, estimated

Tomato40 gin the curries
Cucumber100 gplain salad, first
Hung curd150 gyour own tub from home, instead of canteen curd
Spices3 g

An estimate for a canteen plate built this way:

Office plate: salad first, 1 dry phulka or 75 g rice, 1 katori dal, 1 katori chana, rajma, soya or paneer curry, your 150 g hung curd tub. Nothing fried, no cream gravies, no sweets.

  1. Salad first: a quarter plate of plain cucumber, carrot or onion, with no mayonnaise dressing.
  2. One phulka with no ghee or butter, or half a katori of rice (75 g). Not both.
  3. One katori of dal.
  4. One katori of protein curry: chana, rajma, soya, or paneer with pieces no bigger than a matchbox. No egg curry (your egg is at breakfast) and no chicken (not a chicken day).
  5. Your own 150 g tub of hung curd instead of the canteen curd or raita.
  6. Skip fried food (puri, bhatura, pakora, samosa, fried papad), cream, malai or makhani gravies, sweets and sugary drinks.
  7. If there is no protein curry, take a second half katori of dal and eat 20 g roasted chana from your bag.

20:30

Paneer and soya tikka, charred vegetables, herbed quinoa

25 minutes

500 kcal · 45 g protein · 47 g carbs · 17 g fat · 12 g fibre

Ingredients
ItemWeightNote
Low-fat paneer50 gcut in 4 cubes
Soya chunks (dry)35 gdry weight; soaked 15 min, squeezed
Hung curd30 gtikka marinade
Mustard oil3 gin the marinade
Spices3 gkashmiri chilli, garam masala, kasuri methi
Broccoli80 gflorets
Bell pepper50 gchunks
Zucchini60 ghalf-moons
Mushrooms60 ghalved
Garlic4 g
Olive oil, extra virgin3 gfor the vegetables
Quinoa, cooked75 gfrom the Sunday batch, with chopped coriander; 25 g dry
Hung Curd Garlic Dip40 gon the side
  1. Soak the soya chunks in hot salted water for 15 minutes, then squeeze them dry.
  2. Mix hung curd, mustard oil and spices. Coat the paneer and soya and rest for 10 minutes.
  3. Char on a hot grill pan, or air-fry at 200 °C for 10 to 12 minutes, turning once.
  4. Toss the vegetables with olive oil and garlic and roast in the same pan or air fryer for 10 minutes.
  5. Warm the quinoa with chopped coriander and serve with the garlic dip.

Spinach, sprouted moong and paneer chilla

Prepped last night · 15 minutes

509 kcal · 33 g protein · 57 g carbs · 19 g fat · 16 g fibre

Ingredients
ItemWeightNote
Sprouted moong130 gfrom 54 g dry moong; batter ground last night
Spinach (palak)60 graw, into the batter
Besan (gram flour)15 gbinds the batter
Ginger6 g
Garlic4 g
Green chilli3 g
Spices1 gjeera, ajwain, salt
Low-fat paneer50 gcrumbled, the filling
Onion30 gthe filling
Coriander leaves5 gthe filling
Sunflower oil3 gfor 3 chillas
Signature Guacamole35 gon the side
Almonds10 gabout 8, soaked overnight
  1. Stir the batter you made last night. If it thickened, loosen it with 1 to 2 tbsp water.
  2. Heat a tawa on medium-high and wipe it with 1 g of the oil.
  3. Ladle a third of the batter into the centre and spread it outward in quick circles to about 18 cm. Cook for 2 minutes until the edges lift.
  4. Scatter a third of the paneer filling, press it in, flip for 40 seconds and fold. Make two more the same way.
  5. Serve with the guacamole and eat the soaked almonds.

Kadai soya with peppers and peas, ragi roti

20 minutes

479 kcal · 41 g protein · 61 g carbs · 9 g fat · 17 g fibre

Ingredients
ItemWeightNote
Soya chunks (dry)60 gdry weight; soak 15 min in hot water, squeeze
Everyday Masala Base80 gfrom the Sunday batch
Bell pepper70 gchunks
Green peas25 g
Mustard oil4 g
Spices4 gkadai masala, crushed coriander seed

  1. Soak the soya in hot water for 15 minutes, then squeeze it dry.
  2. Heat the mustard oil with crushed coriander seed. Stir-fry the peppers on high for 3 minutes.
  3. Add the masala base and kadai masala, then the soya and peas. Cook for 5 minutes and finish with coriander.
  4. For the ragi roti, mix the flour and a pinch of salt with hot water to a soft dough. Pat it out between two sheets of butter paper (ragi cracks) and cook on a dry tawa for 1 minute a side.
  5. Serve with the garlic dip and cucumber sticks.

Tandoori chicken burrito bowl

Prepped last night · 20 minutes

563 kcal · 54 g protein · 51 g carbs · 17 g fat · 12 g fibre

Ingredients
ItemWeightNote
Chicken breast, skinless160 graw weight, marinated overnight

  1. Take the chicken out of the fridge 15 minutes ahead.
  2. Cook it in a hot grill pan, or air-fry at 200 °C for 12 to 14 minutes, until it reaches 74 °C inside with no pink. Rest it for 3 minutes, then slice.
  3. Mix the salsa: tomato, onion, coriander and a squeeze of lemon.
  4. Build the bowl: quinoa and chana at the bottom, then lettuce, cabbage, corn, salsa and the chicken. Finish with guacamole and the garlic dip as the crema.

  1. Soak the soya for 15 minutes in hot water and squeeze it dry.
  2. Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 1 minute, plunge it into cold water to keep it green, and blend it with garlic, ginger and chilli.
  3. Heat the mustard oil with jeera, add the masala base, then the spinach purée, and simmer for 4 minutes.
  4. Add the paneer and soya for 3 minutes. Take the pan off the heat and whisk in the hung curd; it splits if it boils. Finish with kasuri methi.

An estimate for a canteen plate built this way:

Office plate: salad first, 1 dry phulka or 75 g rice, 1 katori dal, 1 katori chana, rajma, soya or paneer curry, your 150 g hung curd tub. Nothing fried, no cream gravies, no sweets.

  1. Salad first: a quarter plate of plain cucumber, carrot or onion, with no mayonnaise dressing.
  2. One phulka with no ghee or butter, or half a katori of rice (75 g). Not both.
  3. One katori of dal.
  4. One katori of protein curry: chana, rajma, soya, or paneer with pieces no bigger than a matchbox. No egg curry (your egg is at breakfast) and no chicken (not a chicken day).
  5. Your own 150 g tub of hung curd instead of the canteen curd or raita.
  6. Skip fried food (puri, bhatura, pakora, samosa, fried papad), cream, malai or makhani gravies, sweets and sugary drinks.
  7. If there is no protein curry, take a second half katori of dal and eat 20 g roasted chana from your bag.

The rules

What every day of the plan keeps to, worked out from the gram weights.

  • Calories1,872 to 1,969 kcal every day, inside your 1,800 to 2,000 target.
  • Protein151 to 164 g every day, counting one 30 g scoop of whey (24 g protein) after training.
  • EggsMonday, Wednesday and Friday only: 1 whole egg, the rest whites.
  • ChickenWednesday lunch and Saturday dinner. Never Tuesday or Thursday.
  • FatsOlive, mustard and sunflower oil, 5 to 11 g a day at home, plus nuts, seeds and avocado. Nothing deep-fried; no ghee, butter, cream or trans fats.
  • Saturated fat12.3 to 15.7 g a day, about 7% of calories.
  • Fibre43 to 53 g a day. Drink 3 to 3.5 litres of water to keep up with it.
  • Cholesterol77 to 352 mg a day from food. One yolk is about 186 mg; Wednesday, with both egg and chicken, is the highest. Swap its whole egg for 2 whites to bring it under 200 mg.
  • DrinksBlack coffee at 09:00. At 16:30, water, chaas, sattu or nimbu pani without sugar; no tea or green tea.

Recipes

The six that the week is built on, with this week's exact batch amounts.

Signature Guacamole

Made Sunday (Mon breakfast 45 g, Tue breakfast 35 g, Wed breakfast 40 g, Wed lunch 42 g) and Wednesday (Thu breakfast 40 g, Fri breakfast 45 g, Sat breakfast 40 g, Sat dinner 42 g). Keeps 2 to 3 days.

Hung curd is the signature: it makes the guacamole creamy, adds protein and spreads the avocado's fat further.

Per 100 g: 112 kcal, 2.7 g protein, 8 g carbs, 8.9 g fat, 4.4 g fibre.

IngredientSundayWednesday
Avocado94 g97 g
Hung curd19 g19 g
Onion15 g16 g
Tomato19 g19 g
Coriander leaves4 g about 4 sprigs4 g about 4 sprigs
Green chilli2 g about 1 chilli2 g about 1 chilli
Garlic1 g about ¼ clove1 g about ¼ clove
Lemon juice8 g about 1½ tsp8 g about 1½ tsp
Spices roasted jeera and a pinch of chaat masala, salt1 g a pinch1 g a pinch
  1. Mash the avocado with the lemon juice first; the acid stops it browning.
  2. Fold in the hung curd until smooth.
  3. Add the onion, deseeded tomato, chilli, grated garlic, coriander, roasted jeera, chaat masala and salt.
  4. Pack it into a small airtight box and press cling film onto the surface so no air touches it. Lid on, fridge. If the top darkens, scrape off a millimetre.

Low-Oil Rajma

Made Wednesday night, about 480 g from 77 g dry beans (Thu lunch 250 g, Sat lunch 230 g). Keeps 3 days in the fridge or a month frozen. 1 tsp of oil for the whole batch.

IngredientWednesday
Rajma (dry)77 g
Mustard oil 1 tsp5 g about 1 tsp
Onion72 g
Tomato106 g
Ginger5 g about 1 cm
Garlic5 g about 1 clove
Green chilli2 g about 1 chilli
Spices jeera, kashmiri chilli, dhania, garam masala, haldi6 g about 2 tsp
Coriander leaves4 g about 4 sprigs

Per 100 g: 78 kcal, 4.4 g protein, 13 g carbs, 1.3 g fat, 3.5 g fibre.

  1. Tuesday night, rinse the rajma and soak it in four times its volume of water in the fridge.
  2. Drain and rinse. Pressure-cook with three times its volume of fresh water and salt: one whistle on high, then 15 to 18 minutes on low. A bean must squash easily between two fingers; undercooked kidney beans are unsafe.
  3. Heat the mustard oil until it just smokes, let it cool for 10 seconds, then add jeera and a bay leaf.
  4. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and 2 tbsp water, cover for 4 minutes so it softens in steam, then uncover and cook until golden.
  5. Add ginger, garlic and chilli for a minute, the powdered spices with 2 tbsp water for 30 seconds, then the tomato until it breaks down and darkens, 6 to 8 minutes.
  6. Add the beans and 150 ml of their cooking water. Mash 2 tbsp of beans against the pot: this is the creaminess, instead of butter or cream. Simmer 10 to 15 minutes until thick.
  7. Finish with kasuri methi and coriander. Weigh the batch, cool it within an hour, and box it in portions.

Spinach, Moong and Paneer Chilla

Sprouted moong, spinach, paneer, garlic and ginger. Tuesday breakfast; makes 3 chillas of about 18 cm. Batter ground the night before; 15 minutes in the morning.

IngredientWeight
Sprouted moong from 54 g dry moong; batter ground last night130 g
Spinach (palak) raw, into the batter60 g
Besan (gram flour) binds the batter15 g
Ginger6 g about 1 cm
Garlic4 g about 1 clove
Green chilli3 g about 1½ chillies
Spices jeera, ajwain, salt1 g about ½ tsp
Low-fat paneer crumbled, the filling50 g
Onion the filling30 g
Coriander leaves the filling5 g about 5 sprigs
Sunflower oil for 3 chillas3 g about ¾ tsp
  1. The night before, blend the sprouts, spinach, ginger, garlic and chilli with 50 ml water to a slightly coarse paste. Stir in the besan, jeera, ajwain and salt. It should coat a spoon like thick dosa batter.
  2. Mix the filling: crumbled paneer, finely chopped onion and coriander, a pinch of chaat masala and a squeeze of lemon.
  3. Heat a tawa on medium-high and wipe it with 1 g oil. Ladle a third of the batter into the centre and spread it outward in quick circles.
  4. Cook for 2 minutes, until the edges lift and the top looks dry. Scatter a third of the filling, press it in, flip for 40 seconds and fold. Repeat twice.

Saturday's ragi version. Swap the spinach for 20 g ragi flour and 10 g besan, and stir 30 g grated carrot and 25 g onion into the batter. The same 3 chillas, a nuttier, darker crust.

Hung Curd Garlic Dip

Made Sunday (Mon dinner 40 g, Tue dinner 40 g, Wed lunch 30 g) and Wednesday (Fri dinner 40 g, Sat dinner 40 g). Keeps 3 days.

To hang curd, line a sieve with muslin over a deep bowl, tip in the curd, fold the cloth over and refrigerate for 8 to 10 hours. 1 kg gives about 500 g.

Per 100 g: 90 kcal, 9 g protein, 5 g carbs, 4 g fat, 0.4 g fibre. Keep the whey: knead it into roti dough or use it in the rajma.

IngredientSundayWednesday
Hung curd95 g69 g
Garlic3 g about ¾ clove2 g about ½ clove
Olive oil, extra virgin2 g about ½ tsp2 g about ½ tsp
Mint leaves2 g about 5 leaves2 g about 3 leaves
Coriander leaves2 g about 2 sprigs2 g about 1½ sprigs
Lemon juice5 g about 1 tsp3 g about ¾ tsp
Spices pepper, chilli flakes, salt1 g a pinch1 g a pinch
  1. Grate the garlic, or roast a whole head and squeeze it out for a mellow version.
  2. Whisk it into the hung curd with the olive oil, lemon juice, chopped mint and coriander.
  3. Season with black pepper, chilli flakes and salt. Box and refrigerate.

Everyday Masala Base

Made Sunday (Tue dinner 80 g, Wed breakfast 50 g) and Wednesday (Thu breakfast 60 g, Thu dinner 60 g, Fri dinner 80 g). Keeps 3 days in a glass jar.

One pot of onion-tomato masala on Sunday and Wednesday means every bhurji, kadai and palak on a weekday morning or night starts already cooked.

Per 100 g: 72 kcal, 2 g protein, 12 g carbs, 2.5 g fat, 2.8 g fibre.

IngredientSundayWednesday
Onion78 g120 g
Tomato104 g160 g
Ginger5 g about 1 cm8 g about 1½ cm
Garlic5 g about 1½ cloves8 g about 2 cloves
Green chilli2 g about ¾ chilli2 g about 1 chilli
Mustard oil3 g about ½ tsp4 g about 1 tsp
Spices haldi, dhania, kashmiri chilli, jeera3 g about 1 tsp4 g about 1½ tsp
  1. Heat the mustard oil until it just smokes and let it cool for 10 seconds.
  2. Add the onion with salt and 2 tbsp water; cover for 4 minutes, then cook uncovered until golden.
  3. Add ginger, garlic and chilli for a minute, then haldi, dhania, kashmiri chilli and jeera with a splash of water.
  4. Add the tomato and cook until jammy and deep red, 10 to 12 minutes. Cool, and keep it in a jar.

Tandoori Marinade

Tuesday night for Wednesday lunch; Friday night for Saturday dinner. 8 to 24 hours in the fridge.

Hung curd and lemon tenderise the chicken overnight, so it cooks in 12 minutes without drying out.

IngredientWednesdaySaturday
Chicken breast, skinless160 g190 g
Hung curd30 g30 g
Ginger5 g about 1 cm5 g about 1 cm
Garlic5 g about 1 clove5 g about 1 clove
Lemon juice10 g about 2 tsp10 g about 2 tsp
Mustard oil4 g about 1 tsp4 g about 1 tsp
Spices tandoori masala4 g about 1½ tsp4 g about 1½ tsp
  1. Slash the breast 3 or 4 times. Rub in lemon juice, salt and kashmiri chilli and leave it for 10 minutes.
  2. Mix the hung curd, ginger, garlic, mustard oil and tandoori masala; coat the chicken. Cover and refrigerate.
  3. Cook in a hot grill pan or air fryer at 200 °C for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until it reads 74 °C in the thickest part.

Batch prep

Two sessions with the chef, Sunday and Wednesday night, plus three strainings of curd. Every batch is sized to what the week eats, so nothing is left over.

The basics

CurdHang curd

Line a sieve with muslin over a deep bowl. Tip in the low-fat curd, fold the cloth over and refrigerate for 8 to 10 hours. 1 kg gives about 500 g. Keep the whey for roti dough or the rajma pot.

SproutsSprout moong

Soak whole moong for 8 to 10 hours. Drain, rinse, and tie it in a damp muslin cloth or a sprouter somewhere warm and dark. Rinse morning and evening. Tails of 3 to 5 mm in 12 to 24 hours; refrigerate then, and steam for 3 minutes before eating.

ChanaBoil kala chana

Soak 8 to 12 hours. Pressure-cook in three times its volume of fresh water with salt, 6 to 7 whistles. Tender but whole. Drain, cool and box.

QuinoaCook quinoa

Rinse in a fine sieve until the water runs clear (this removes the bitter coating). Simmer covered in twice its volume of water for 15 minutes, rest 5, fluff with a fork.

RiceCook brown rice

Soak for 30 minutes. Pressure-cook in 2.5 times its volume of water, 3 whistles. Spread it on a plate to cool, refrigerate within an hour, and reheat until steaming.

NutsSoak almonds and walnuts

Every night, 10 g almonds (about 8) in a katori of water for the next breakfast; peel them in the morning. Walnuts soak the same way the night before Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday.

Shopping

Two shops a week, Sunday and Wednesday. Only chicken and milk are bought fresh, the evening before. Quantities are the exact weights the plan uses.

Sunday: pantry for the week

Plus a spice shelf check: jeera, ajwain, haldi, dhania powder, kashmiri chilli, garam masala, kasuri methi, tandoori, kadai and keema masala, chaat masala, black salt, black pepper, chilli flakes, bay leaves.

Notes

How the numbers were made

Every figure is calculated from the gram weights on this page, using USDA FoodData Central and the Indian Food Composition Tables (IFCT 2017). Weights are raw or dry unless the item says boiled, cooked or sprouted. The office lunch is an estimate of a plate built by the rules. Labels on paneer, tofu, bread and whey vary by brand; check yours, and swap like for like.

Food safety

  • Rajma. Raw kidney beans contain a toxin that only full boiling destroys. Pressure-cook until a bean squashes easily between two fingers, and never slow-cook rajma from raw.
  • Sprouts. Steam sprouts for 3 minutes before eating them raw, refrigerate once the tails show, and use them within 3 days.
  • Cooked rice and quinoa. Spread them out to cool, refrigerate within an hour, keep them for no more than 3 days, and reheat until steaming hot.
  • Chicken. Marinate in the fridge, never on the counter. Cook to 74 °C in the thickest piece, with clear juices and no pink.
  • Packed snacks. Curd and paneer boxes go in an insulated bag with an ice pack, or straight into the office fridge.

Tracking progress

Aim for a steady 0.5 to 0.75 kg a week. Weigh yourself once a week: same morning, after the bathroom, before coffee. If the scale has not moved for two weeks, take out 100 to 150 kcal (one roti, or a teaspoon of oil) and keep protein where it is. If you lose more than 1 kg a week for three weeks running, add a piece of fruit.

Your doctor

This plan is built around cholesterol-friendly eating, not medical treatment. If you take medicine for cholesterol, blood pressure or blood sugar, show it to your doctor, and recheck your lipid profile after 8 to 12 weeks.

The plan repeats every week. Saturday night sets up Sunday; Sunday sets up Monday.

Printed, each day takes its own page.
